messages.subject: Differences.bootstrap warnings
parts:
Hello distance sampler,

Here I am again for what I hope will be my final question in the context of my analyses.

A few weeks ago, Eric, you advised me to use the differences.bootstrap function for the statistical comparison of densities obtained between the study areas I am investigating. After conducting various analyses and finding the model that best fits my data, I tried to use the function, but I am getting numerous warnings in the process regarding the function not being strictly monotonic. Of course, when fitting the model individually, I do not get any such warnings.

I would like to know if, despite the warnings, I can consider the results I obtain reliable and include them in the final outcomes, or if based on the nature and amount of data available to me, it would be better to avoid this type of analysis because it is too imprecise.

I am attaching the data, my code, the warnings I am getting, and the resulting graph from the function.

Thank you very much for your help. Have a great day, Riccardo.

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Differences.bootstrap warnings
parts:
Riccardo

The bootstrap approach, while valid, is not particularly appropriate for your situation. Until I reviewed your data, I had forgotten your design had only two replicate transects per stratum. Because sampling with replacement is performed by the bootstrap at the level of transects; the number of unique combinations, and hence unique differences in density is small (<10). As a consequence, the resulting distribution of estimated differences produced by the bootstrap does not have a nice shape (contrast the histogram from your email with the histogram shown in the case study):

Hence, I would suggest the bootstrap is more than is necessary for your analysis from your small study. I'm uncertain why you have chosen to truncate 20% of your data; truncating 5% is customary for line transect data and there is a natural break in the detection distances around 125m.

The encounter rate in PNFC is larger than the encounter rate in SR by a factor of almost 3. If you use a pooled detection function (common detection function for both strata), this results in a density for PNFC that is roughly 3X larger than the density in SR. I don't think you'll want to perform more formal statistical comparison with the design implemented.

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Differences.bootstrap warnings
parts:
Riccardo

AIC is of no use in determining truncation distance; AIC values are not comparable when comparing different data sets (truncation changes the data).

AIC could help determine whether a more complex model (separate detection functions for each stratum) is preferable to a simpler model (strata share a common detection function). This contrast is described in our online training material: slides 11 and 12 of
https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/lecturepdfs/Ch5/L5-2%20Stratification.pdf

You will need to do some of the AIC calculation for the separate detection function model by hand.
